# Mount Logan Expands Interval Fund Platform with Proposed AFA Asset Based Lending Fund Transaction


October 20, 2026 8:00am EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_40aaf19935c0678f9b1b027ad22329dc/mountlogancapital/news/2026-10-20_Mount_Logan_Expands_Interval_Fund_Platform_with_128.pdf)


***Mount Logan Management LLC has signed a definitive agreement to succeed Alternative Fund Advisors, LLC as investment adviser to the AFA Asset Based Lending Fund, which will bring Mount Logan’s interval fund assets under management to approximately $460 million.***


***Once the transaction closes, the Fund will be renamed Mount Logan Asset Based Lending Fund and will continue its focus on asset-based and specialty finance investing. The Fund’s shareholders will gain access to a larger asset management platform and increased direct origination of lending opportunities.***


***Mount Logan currently expects the transaction will be immediately accretive to its FRE*** ***1*** ***upon closing.***


***The transaction is expected to close in Q1 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.***


NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mount Logan Capital Inc. (Nasdaq: MLCI) (“Mount Logan”) today announced that Mount Logan Management LLC, its wholly owned registered investment adviser ("MLM"), has entered into a definitive agreement to become the new investment adviser to the AFA Asset Based Lending Fund (“Fund”) (the “Transaction”). In connection with the Transaction, MLM and Alternative Fund Advisors, LLC (“AFA”), the Fund’s current investment adviser, have entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (the "APA") pursuant to which MLM will acquire certain business records, intellectual property, and goodwill of AFA related to the management of the Fund.


The Fund will be MLM’s second evergreen credit interval fund, complementing MLM’s Opportunistic Credit Interval Fund. Together, the two funds establish a scaled, differentiated product suite for the private wealth channel, spanning asset-based specialty finance and opportunistic corporate credit.


Upon closing, the Fund will be renamed Mount Logan Asset Based Lending Fund. It will continue to provide access to a broadly diversified range of asset-based lending and specialty finance credits. Fund shareholders are expected to benefit from MLM’s scale, resources and extensive in-house origination capability. The Fund manages approximately $230 million in assets from a wide range of investors, particularly those interested in diversifying their fixed income portfolios.


The Transaction will bring MLM’s combined interval fund assets to approximately $460 million. Mount Logan currently expects the Transaction will be immediately accretive to FRE upon closing.


**Ted Goldthorpe, CEO of Mount Logan** , said, "This is a significant milestone in the build-out of Mount Logan's evergreen credit platform and reflects our continued discipline in acquiring permanent and semi-permanent capital vehicles. The Fund broadens MLM's core products, extends our distribution reach in the private wealth channel, and is highly complementary to our Opportunistic Credit Interval Fund. It also provides a differentiated, institutionally managed asset-based lending strategy that leverages the credit sourcing and underwriting capabilities of the broader Mount Logan and BC Partners Credit platform."


“We are excited about this next phase in the evolution of the AFA Asset Based Lending Fund," said **Marco Hanig, CEO of Alternative Fund Advisors** . “We expect the resources and investment expertise of the Mount Logan platform to enhance the Fund’s strategy through direct origination alongside third-party origination channels. We look forward to partnering with Ted and the Mount Logan team in the Fund's next phase of growth.”


**About Mount Logan Capital Inc.**
Mount Logan Capital Inc. (“MLCI”) is an integrated alternative asset management and insurance solutions firm focused on generating durable, fee-based revenue and long-term value creation. MLCI leverages differentiated investment strategies alongside permanent insurance capital to deliver attractive, risk-adjusted returns across market cycles.


Through its subsidiaries, MLM and Ability Insurance Company, MLCI manages and invests across private and public credit markets in North America and operates an insurance platform that provides long-duration liabilities to support its credit investment strategies. This integrated platform is designed to provide stable earnings, downside protection, and a low risk of principal impairment through the credit cycle.


As of June 30, 2026, MLCI had over $2 billion in assets under management.


**About AFA Asset Based Lending Fund**
The AFA Asset Based Lending Fund is an interval fund launched on June 30, 2021 that seeks high current income by investing in a diversified portfolio of asset-based loans across specialty finance, real estate, and other private credit niches. The Fund offers daily subscriptions at net asset value and conducts quarterly repurchase offers subject to a limit of 5% of the Fund’s net assets. As of September 30, 2026, the Fund had approximately $230 million in net assets across 650 underlying investments.


**About Alternative Fund Advisors, LLC**
Alternative Fund Advisors provides financial advisors and family offices with efficient and convenient access to private investments through interval funds.


**Approvals and Timing**
Additional details regarding the Transaction are available on a Current Report on Form 8-K that was filed by Mount Logan with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) at www.sec.gov. The Transaction has been unanimously approved by the AFA Asset Based Lending Fund’s board of trustees, as well as Mount Logan’s board of directors. The change in investment adviser and the new investment management agreement are subject to approval by a majority of the Fund’s shareholders, as well as customary regulatory approvals. The Fund intends to file a proxy statement with the SEC shortly following this announcement and thereafter commence the shareholder vote solicitation. Subject to the requisite approvals, closing is expected to occur in Q1 2027.


**Advisors**
Dechert LLP is serving as legal counsel to Mount Logan. Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath LLP is serving as legal counsel to the AFA Asset Based Lending Fund and its Board of Trustees. Reitler Kailas & Rosenblatt LLP is serving as legal counsel and Berkshire Global Advisors is serving as financial advisor to AFA.

AFA ASSET BASED LENDING FUND DISCLOSURES


The Fund’s quarterly repurchase offer is expected to be 5% of net assets, but may range from 5% to 25% subject to approval by the Fund’s Board of Trustees. If a repurchase offer is oversubscribed, shareholders will only be able to have a portion of their shares repurchased. There is no guarantee that shareholders will be able to tender their shares when or in the amount they desire.


**Investors should carefully consider the Fund’s investment objectives, risks, charges, and expenses before investing. This information is included in the Fund Prospectus which can be accessed at https://alternativefundadvisors.com or by calling 800-452-6804. Read the prospectus carefully before you invest.**


An investment in the Fund involves a high degree of risk. An investment in the Fund should be viewed only as part of an overall investment program and you should invest only if you can sustain a complete loss of your principal. An investment in the Fund is subject to, among others, the following risks:


- The Fund is a “non-diversified” management investment company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended;
- Shares of the Fund are not listed on any securities exchange and it is not anticipated that a secondary market for shares will develop;
- Shares are appropriate only for those investors who can tolerate a high degree of risk and do not require a liquid investment;
- Although the Fund will offer quarterly liquidity through a quarterly repurchase process, there is no assurance that an investor will be able to sell or otherwise liquidate all their shares tendered during a quarterly repurchase offer; and
- The Fund’s investment in private credit companies is speculative and involves a high degree of risk, including the risk associated with leverage.
